name: How a comparison is drawn
caption: Comparison plots show treatment minus baseline and a 95% interval. The example is legacy → Cartesian codec, +0.29 [+0.08,+0.51], over 96 paired boots. Recipe comparisons can change multiple things; those limits are stated locally. Capacity plots show absolute scores. Intervals describe evaluation uncertainty, not training-seed variation.

name: Loss and play across one training run
caption: The 216M Muon production run (O50). Top: validation negative log-likelihood every 4,096 updates. Bottom: net stocks per minute at each of the 16 checkpoints that were played, 96 two-minute episodes each, with a 95% interval. Play rose to +0.16 at 24,576 updates and fell to −0.18 at 57,344 while the loss held near 1.44, then climbed to +0.34 as the loss fell to 1.38. Checkpoints are picked by play.

name: The policy, end to end
caption: Observation → frame token → history → action decoder → controller → game. The new game state and applied controller frame feed the next observation. Detailed encodings, head wiring and timing are shown separately.

name: The five stages, on one time axis
caption: Time runs left to right; the hierarchy runs down. The observation encoder makes one token per observed frame; the trunk attends back over the 128 frames it has seen and ends in the current state hₜ, which is the only state that drives the plan. To the right of now, the temporal decoder's ten steps sit at the offsets they predict, 1–6, 9, 12, 16 and 20 frames ahead, and each step picks the four controller groups in order. The runtime sends only the t+1 frame; the other nine offsets never reach Dolphin and shape the trunk in training. Configuration and parameter counts are the 15,053,039-parameter O43 model. Select a stage to inspect its shapes, parameters and configuration.

name: What a predicted action is given
caption: The four O37 cells, same parameters, data, updates and deployment. Across-frame conditioning hands the decoder the frames it has already written; within-frame conditioning hands each controller group the groups already chosen in that frame. Each cell is shown as the unconditioned cell → that cell with a 95% interval. Averaged over the other axis, adding across-frame conditioning was worth +0.36 [+0.23, +0.49] stocks/min and +13.5 [+5.1, +22.0] damage/min; adding within-frame conditioning +0.25 [+0.14, +0.36] and +8.5 [+0.6, +16.5].

name: Decoding one action chunk
caption: Each decoder token is the embedded previous frame, the trunk state hₜ and the frame offset k. The tokens pass through a causal self-attention block over the earlier chunk tokens, a cross-attention to keys and values projected once from every trunk state in the context, further causal blocks and a norm into the frame state; the four heads of {{fig:action-logit-paths}} then write that frame, and the written frame embeds into the next token. Training runs every step at once with the true prefix; play runs the steps in order with cached keys and values.

name: Inside one written frame
caption: One decoder token per future frame, (hₜ, previous written frame, offset), through two causal attention blocks; each frame’s four heads then fire in order, C-stick first. Later heads see the picks made so far through FiLM on the frame state; every head is a norm → linear → SiLU → linear stack whose logits also receive a linear skip from the trunk state hₜ. O43 tested each part against the model without it: zero-init FiLM → ordinary init +1.09 [+0.75, +1.43] stocks/min, no trunk skip → trunk skip +0.89 [+0.49, +1.29], linear head → SiLU MLP head +2.03 [+1.75, +2.31] on the character suite; the Fox suite agrees. Hover a row to light the part.

name: Run-length action spans
caption: O18 packed the four controller groups into one symbol per frame and let BPE merge repeated holds into span tokens of up to 16 frames. The compression was real; executing a token to completion was not, and the package lost 2.6 stocks per minute.

name: The observation token
caption: Every source of one token. Player blocks carry a validity mask; an absent follower is all zeros with its mask set. The four projectile slots share one encoder whose output is multiplied by the slot’s presence flag before the sum, so an empty slot adds exactly zero and order does not matter. Characters, stage and the player identity are embedded directly. The previous controller frame enters as the classes the decoder predicts, each class carrying its learned embedding and the physical stick or trigger value.

name: Reward, return and weight, frame by frame
caption: A replay segment around a stock loss illustrates how the return half-life changes earlier weights. The moving-average or game-mean baseline is a substitute, not the learned O52 value estimate. Displayed weights are unnormalized; O52 normalizes eligible weights across the batch. Reward parameters default to O52 values. Expand settings to change the game, baseline, beta, cap or time range.

name: Past-action encoding
caption: The previous controller frame as a 256-way one-hot class against the class embedding plus a linear map of its physical stick and trigger values. One-hot → learned: +0.26 [+0.08, +0.44] stocks/min, +23.7 [+13.8, +33.6] damage/min, despite fewer examples and fewer parameters.

name: The shard loader
caption: Shards are read once, in an order fixed for the run. Each replay is decoded once into W windows (context plus chunk) at different starts and enters a FIFO ring of C slots; every batch of B windows draws each window from a different replay. Window k of a replay is used about k·P batches after the replay entered, P = C/B, jittered inside a phase block, so one replay's windows are ≈ P batches apart and never share a batch. O52: W = 8, C = 112,128, B = 512, P = 219, phase block 25, so consecutive windows are 195–243 batches apart. The checkpoint stores the cursor and one locator per slot, not the decoded arrays.

name: Other objectives against behavior cloning
caption: Behavior cloning → each alternative, with a 95% interval. Attached IQL: −2.01 [−2.22, −1.81] stocks/min. Causal decoder → endpoint flow: −0.19 [−0.38, +0.00] stocks/min and −33.0 [−44.6, −21.4] damage/min with more compute. Exploration modeling: −1.68 [−1.95, −1.40] with one plan, −0.81 [−0.98, −0.63] with eight.

name: Advantage weighting
caption: Behavior cloning → AWR: +0.08 [−0.10, +0.26] stocks/min, +10.8 [−1.4, +23.0] damage/min; the two evaluations were not paired (96 and 128 boots), so the interval combines the two arms' standard errors. Return half-life 3 s → 8 s: +0.37 [+0.19, +0.54] stocks/min; 3 s → 14 s: +0.32 [+0.16, +0.48].

name: Windows per replay in one batch
caption: The illustration holds batch size at 16 windows: four replays with four windows each versus sixteen replays with one window each. The actual matched training comparison used batch 1,024. Four → one window per replay gave +0.73 [−0.07,+1.53] stocks/min with wide uncertainty under the old evaluation.

name: Frames played before replanning
caption: Each O37 checkpoint at 1, 2, 4 and 6 frames per plan, as 1 frame → each setting with a 95% interval. 1 → 6 frames: −1.00 [−1.20, −0.81] stocks/min for the cell conditioned on nothing, −0.07 [−0.23, +0.08] for the cell conditioned on frames and groups. Execution length and replan interval change together, so this is not a replan-only result.

name: Batch size at fixed data
caption: Batch size at a fixed 2.1 million examples, batch 2,048 → each arm with a 95% interval. Every arm saw the same data, so a smaller batch simply bought more optimizer updates. 2,048 → 128: +0.47 [+0.25, +0.69] stocks/min. One seed.

name: The learning-rate pair
caption: The Muon and AdamW rates move together as one pair; the smallest pair → each arm with a 95% interval. .014 / .000595 → .040 / .00170 gains +0.22 [+0.02, +0.42] stocks/min and sits inside the sweep, but its neighbours are not separated from it.

name: Controller codecs
caption: Legacy emits one button per frame and one fused shoulder value with five targets; Cartesian and polar emit an 8-bit button mask and keep L and R separate, five targets each, and differ in how the main stick is quantised.

name: Codec comparisons
caption: Legacy → Cartesian: +0.29 [+0.08, +0.51] stocks/min, +16.3 [+3.4, +29.1] damage/min. Cartesian → polar: +0.10 [−0.08, +0.28] stocks/min, +0.9 [−10.8, +12.6] damage/min.

name: Player identity
caption: Each identity is compared with masked identity. Cody and Mang0 identify individual players; Master and Platinum are pooled ranked-player identities. Cody changes damage more clearly than stocks. Evaluation uncertainty is shown for both metrics.

name: Optimizer and rate recipe
caption: Each row changes the optimizer and its learning rates together, so this is a recipe comparison, not a pure algorithm test. Early 7M test, AdamW → Muon + AdamW: +0.03 [−0.77, +0.83] stocks/min under the old, unpaired evaluation. Production 216M run, Muon + AdamW → all AdamW: +0.15 [−0.03, +0.33] stocks/min, +15.2 [+2.8, +27.5] damage/min. Muon reached the lower validation loss in the small test; AdamW did in production.

name: One data source or all 44
caption: Ranked-anonymized replays only → the natural mix of all 44 sources, same architecture and update count: −0.06 [−0.22, +0.10] stocks/min, +6.3 [−4.8, +17.4] damage/min. No clear gameplay gain from the wider mix in this test.

name: Where the loss goes
caption: The decoder predicts ten frames at offsets 1–6, 9, 12, 16 and 20. O26 gave the four near frames one unit of loss between them and the six far frames another. The tested split gives the next frame a whole unit and spreads the second over the other nine. O26 split → half on the next frame, same legacy codec and O43 architecture: +0.14 [−0.08, +0.36] stocks/min, +3.7 [−10.0, +17.3] damage/min. Positive, but not separated from zero.

name: Supervising every position, or only the last
caption: O52 trains the decoder at each of the last 128 positions of a 256-frame window; O55 trains it only at the final position, with the same windows, updates, model and data. Dense → sparse (A): −1.12 [−1.31, −0.93] stocks/min. Inside the sparse setup, against A: adding one history cross-attention layer (B) +0.06 [−0.11, +0.25]; adding it and removing the trunk-state input (C) −0.05 [−0.23, +0.12]; replacing the decoder's action self-attention with history attention and removing the trunk-state input (D) −0.11 [−0.31, +0.09]. Every arm keeps the direct trunk-to-logit skip. Paired bootstrap over 96 shared boots. Cross-attention on a densely supervised decoder was not trained.

name: Ideas that did not pan out
caption: Completed tests with no demonstrated gain, followed by unfinished or inconclusive work. Differences describe the tested systems, with paired or unpaired evaluation intervals. Other changes in each row limit component-level causal interpretation. An interval crossing zero is not a strong rejection.

name: Bytes per corpus, before and after the compact layout
caption: The ranked corpus uses 802.47 GB of decoded training arrays in the old format versus 76.19 GB in the compact layout, 10.5× smaller. The compressed artifact is 29.82 → 13.34 GB, shown separately as text. No matched throughput benchmark is claimed.

name: Real-time chunking
caption: By the time a plan returns, the game already holds the next d actions in its input queue. Real-time chunking (O46) hands those d actions back to the decoder as a fixed prefix and writes only the frames after them, so a new plan agrees with what is about to happen; training draws d at random from 0 to 4 at every step and puts no loss on the prefix. The one retained treatment run, c6yd7zxx, stopped at 4,096 updates (−1.17 stocks/min on the character suite, −0.62 on the Fox suite) and its planned dense control was never run, so the idea is unresolved, not rejected.

name: Model size against its own delay, at four data budgets
caption: O54: four pure behavior-cloning models (5M, 39M, 125M and 289M parameters), each deployed at the delay its inference forces (1, 2, 3 and 6 frames), trained through nested data budgets of 2²⁸ to 2³¹ supervised positions. Each dot is that model's own score against the CPU, not a difference; all 16 evaluations use the same 96 match-ups, and intervals are 95% boot-cluster percentiles. At 2³¹ the 125M model at 3 frames is highest, −0.01 [−0.12, +0.09] stocks/min; the 289M model reaches a lower imitation loss but plays at −0.42 [−0.54, −0.29]. Size and delay move together, so this is a deployment frontier, not a size effect.

name: Predicting the next data budget
caption: Separate models are fitted through D30 and evaluated at D31. Hollow points are predictions at D31; prediction uncertainty is not shown. Filled points and 95% intervals are observed scores. The predicted ranking failed, so the fits are not used to choose a winner at larger budgets.

name: Validation loss against model size and data
caption: O39: 33 completed runs, five data budgets, seven model sizes. The fit uses all measured points; none were held out. The left panel shows measured loss and fitted data curves. The right panel shows predicted fixed-compute minima under C=6ND. Solid compute segments require both N and D inside the observed ranges; dashed segments extrapolate. Expand the residual panel to inspect measured minus fitted loss. The dedicated O48 study was canceled.
